>Where would I even start?
The best way to learn programming is by start doing it. There are infinite tutorials on youtube and it's even more easy to learn with chatgpt since it can explain thing in every way possible.
Subscribe to some programming channels on YouTube. Make it a daily habit to watch one or two programming videos. At the same time, work on small games, websites, or whatever else you'd like to build.

>There are so many languages.
It depends on what you want to develop. Different languages are partly good for different things. I think you should start with C#. It's a sweet spot between many different things and it's super comfy to use. If you learn to program well in one language, learning other languages later won't be much of a challenge.

>Don't I need Calc and Linear Algebra and beyond?
Not necessarily. You only need math if you go low level, or computer graphics, or AI.

>What theory do I learn?
Search for "code smells" or "clean code principles". You will find a lot of useful sites.

Programming isn't about learning programming languages. A language is just a tool. The essence of programming is being able to independently break down complex problems into smaller parts and solve them step by step, producing a readable and maintainable codebase.
You also need to learn how to find information on your own. A huge part of programming involves research and gathering information relevant to the problem you're trying to solve.
